symbols.name: support
symbols.meaning: The set of coordinates at which a binary vector is 1.
symbols.quote: For a binary vector $z$, $\mathrm{supp}(z)$ is the set of coordinates at which $z$ is $1$, and $\mathrm{wt}(z)=|\mathrm{supp}(z)|$ is its Hamming weight, the number of such coordinates read as an integer.

symbols.name: Hamming weight
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates at which a binary vector is 1, read as an integer.
symbols.quote: For a binary vector $z$, $\mathrm{supp}(z)$ is the set of coordinates at which $z$ is $1$, and $\mathrm{wt}(z)=|\mathrm{supp}(z)|$ is its Hamming weight, the number of such coordinates read as an integer.

symbols.name: integer representative
symbols.meaning: The integer 0 or 1 that represents a field element b of the binary field.
symbols.quote: For $b\in\mathbb F_2$, $[b]\in\{0,1\}$ is its integer representative.

symbols.name: normalized Hadamard matrix
symbols.meaning: The 2 by 2 matrix whose tensor powers give the frames of the phase network.
symbols.quote: The complex phase network computes its frames by the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) $H^{\otimes m}$ of $H=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, the normalized Hadamard matrix; here $H$ denotes this matrix, not the address chunk of other pages.

symbols.name: phase exponent
symbols.meaning: The phase exponent of an address x under label U, the Hamming weight of its projection modulo 4.
symbols.quote: The phase exponent of an address $x$ is $q_U(x)=\mathrm{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4$.

symbols.name: phase frame
symbols.meaning: The frame of a vertex with label U, an operator on arrays of addresses.
symbols.quote: The frame at a vertex with label $U$, the operator $C_U$, is

symbols.name: projection onto W
symbols.meaning: The projection onto a nondegenerate subspace W along its orthogonal complement.
symbols.quote: For a nondegenerate subspace $W$, $P_W$ is the projection onto $W$ along $W^\perp$.

symbols.name: diagonal operator
symbols.meaning: The operator that multiplies the value at each address x by f(x).
symbols.quote: For a function $f$ on addresses, $\mathrm{diag}_x(f(x))$ is the diagonal operator that multiplies the value at each address $x$ by $f(x)$.

symbols.name: tail label
symbols.meaning: The label at the tail of an edge.
symbols.quote: Each vertex carries one label $U$, a subspace of $\mathbb F_2^m$ with $U\cap U^\perp=0$, where $U^\perp$ is the orthogonal complement; such a subspace is nondegenerate.

symbols.name: head label
symbols.meaning: The label at the head of an edge.
symbols.quote: An edge runs from a tail label $U$ to a head label $V$, and its frame change is $C_VC_U^{-1}$.

symbols.name: orthogonal sum
symbols.meaning: A B means that A and B are orthogonal subspaces meeting only in zero, with A+B their orthogonal sum.
symbols.quote: Write $A\perp B$ when every vector of $A$ is orthogonal to every vector of $B$ and $A\cap B=0$, so that $A+B$ is their orthogonal sum.

symbols.name: orthogonal residual
symbols.meaning: The orthogonal complement of the smaller label of an edge inside the larger one.
symbols.quote: The orthogonal residual $\Delta$ of an edge is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one.

symbols.name: orthonormal basis
symbols.meaning: An orthonormal basis of the orthogonal residual, a set of vectors v with v dot v equal to 1 that are pairwise orthogonal.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal O$ be an orthonormal basis of $\Delta$, a set of vectors $v$ with $v\cdot v=1$ and $v\cdot v'=0$ for distinct $v,v'\in\mathcal O$.

symbols.name: edge sign
symbols.meaning: The sign in {1, -1} that matches the weight of basis vector v on an edge, up to sign for the edge direction.
symbols.quote: Let $\varepsilon_v\in\{1,-1\}$ with $\varepsilon_v\equiv\mathrm{wt}(v)\pmod 4$ on an increasing edge and $\varepsilon_v\equiv-\mathrm{wt}(v)\pmod 4$ on a decreasing edge.

symbols.name: first kernel coefficient
symbols.meaning: The complex number (1+i)/2, the diagonal coefficient of a two-point kernel.
symbols.quote: Set $\tau_0=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $\tau_1=\frac{1-i}{2}$; here $\tau$ names these coefficients, not the exponent of the address-interchange page.

symbols.name: second kernel coefficient
symbols.meaning: The complex number (1-i)/2, the off-diagonal coefficient of a two-point kernel.
symbols.quote: Set $\tau_0=\frac{1+i}{2}$ and $\tau_1=\frac{1-i}{2}$; here $\tau$ names these coefficients, not the exponent of the address-interchange page.

symbols.name: translation by v
symbols.meaning: The operator sending a function f to (X_v f)(x) = f(x+v) on addresses.
symbols.quote: For a binary vector $v$ (the letter $v$ names vectors here, not the vertices of other pages), $X_v$ is the translation by $v$ on functions of addresses.

symbols.name: two-point kernel
symbols.meaning: The operator tau_0 I + tau_1 X_v, one factor of an edge change.
symbols.quote: Call $K_v=\tau_0 I+\tau_1 X_v$ the two-point kernel for $v$.

symbols.name: route label
symbols.meaning: The label span(e_1, ..., e_delta) on the route from {0} to the full space.
symbols.quote: For general $m$, take the route $U_0=\{0\}$ and $U_\delta=\mathrm{span}(e_1,\dots,e_\delta)$ for $1\le\delta\le m$, where $e_\delta$ is the standard basis vector with a single $1$ at position $\delta$.

symbols.name: standard basis vector
symbols.meaning: The vector with a single 1 at position delta.
symbols.quote: For general $m$, take the route $U_0=\{0\}$ and $U_\delta=\mathrm{span}(e_1,\dots,e_\delta)$ for $1\le\delta\le m$, where $e_\delta$ is the standard basis vector with a single $1$ at position $\delta$.

relations.quote: The complex phase network is built on the [subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md), with each wire carrying an array of complex values instead of a scalar.
The complex phase network has coefficients in [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), since each such entry is a Gaussian integer divided by $2^m$.
The complex phase network is indexed by [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md).
The complex phase network takes its addresses from the [binary field](binary-field.md), in which addition is exclusive or.

The complex phase network computes its frames by the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) $H^{\otimes m}$ of $H=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, the normalized Hadamard matrix; here $H$ denotes this matrix, not the address chunk of other pages.
The complex phase network checks nondegeneracy with the [Gram matrix](gram-matrix.md) of each label, the matrix of dot products of a basis of $U$.
